messages:
sara: quick brain dump — prototyping a lightweight "soft fallback queue" shim between frontdoor and admission to avoid hard drops during short spikes. idea: fast admit path unchanged; when we detect transient scarcity, frontdoor enqueues minimal metadata to a local FIFO and returns a 202+poll handle. workers drain FIFO at a lower-priority lane. keeps clients alive and lets us smooth bursts without global token churn.

kyle: nice. a couple questions: how long do we hold the handle? client-visible latency SLO?

sara: thinking 5s default, tunable by route. goal is to preserve sub-200ms for fast path; slow-path can be 1-10s depending on policy. handle TTL + optimistic requeue if worker sees capacity.

anika: how do we avoid abuse? enqueues are cheap so abusive clients might flood FIFO to bypass rate limits. need admission checks on enqueue and per-client queuing limits. also consider signed handles + HMAC so clients can't spoof.

kyle: agreed. propose these constraints: per-client enqueue cap, global FIFO depth cap (per-region), enqueue cost charged to tenant (token debit), and ephemeral lease returned so workers can claim without additional auth.

sara: exactly. sketch of minimal transport proto: 
```proto
message SoftFallbackHandle {
  string handle_id = 1;
  string client_id = 2;
  int64 enqueue_ts = 3;
  enum Priority { HIGH=0; MED=1; LOW=2; }
  Priority p = 4;
  bytes sig = 5; // HMAC over (handle_id, client_id, ttl)
}
```

mike: rough tradeoffs: + fewer 429 spikes, + smoother upstream load, - added client poll complexity, - potential tail latencies and complexity in telemetry. Are we ok adding another success path variant in SDKs?

sara: SDK changes minimal — SDK will auto-poll with exponential jitter and surface a single "in_progress" state to apps. Server-side we need a claim endpoint for workers: `POST /claim` with handle.

anika: telemetry items: enqueue_rate by client, claim_latency, dequeue_failures, handle_expiries, spoof_rejects. need to connect these to quality regressions/rollouts in Console.

infra-bot: deploy note: if we shard FIFOs by edge node, we must ensure worker affinity or cross-node transfer costs. recommend per-edge small FIFO + 1 cross-region overflow queue as fallback.

kyle: subtle interface boundary: admission currently expects immediate token debit and response. with fallback, we need a clear contract: (1) admit immediate (SUCCESS), (2) fallback accepted (ENQUEUED + handle), (3) reject (THROTTLED). Migration plan: dry-run mode where frontdoor emits events but still returns 429s — that lets us collect telemetry.

sara: migration plan OK. also need a way to surface fairness: enqueued items should observe per-tenant weight so workers pop proportional to weights (not pure FIFO) — hybrid reservoir across priorities.

anika: does this interact poorly with KV cache (kvcache) warmups? e.g., long-delayed requests may miss cached short prefixes. probably acceptable but worth flagging for ML-surface workloads.

mike: edge-case: what if a worker claims handle but fails to complete (OOM/crash)? need two-phase claim: claim(lease) and then complete/abort. lease TTL + automatic re-enqueue or drop. Also record idempotency keys.

sara: yep: claim returns lease_id, worker sends complete(lease_id, result). on lease expiry handle becomes re-enqueueable with a retry_count. cap retries to avoid hot loops.

kyle: policy knobs: enqueue_cost_tokens, max_enqueues_per_client_per_min, priority_escalation_window, lease_ttl, retry_limit. We should keep defaults conservative.

anika: ops checklist: dashboards for queue depth, per-tenant enqueue cost billing, alert on >5% expiry rate, and anomaly detector for sudden enqueue spikes from single client.

sara: next steps: I'll open an RFC with proposed proto, ingress changes, SDK sketch, telemetry events, and a dry-run rollout plan. tagging @kyle @anika for review before I send to platform-arch.

kyle: LGTM for rough sketch. add a short security section about signed handles and replay protections.

anika: add a note about fairness algorithms — include both weighted-round-robin and reservoir sampling fallback. provide perf microbench targets.

mike: can we prototype in a feature branch with per-edge FIFO + local worker consumer? happy to help with perf harness.

sara: awesome — will carve out a prototyping ticket and ping ops. thanks all :rocket:
